_what: The HELD-OUT third of the door-shelter survey. Every row was read off UT's own building photograph the same way the training rows in scripts/bake_entrances.py SHELTER_OBS were, on the same day, by the same eye - and then withheld from the bake so that 'no canopy unless a photograph shows one' is tested on buildings the bake has never seen.
_why_this_file_exists: A table the bake reads and the meter scores is a tautology: the bake would agree with it by construction. This third is the part that cannot be agreed with by construction. campusmeter.mjs asserts that scripts/bake_entrances.py's SHELTER_OBS and this file are DISJOINT and exits 1 if a code appears in both - which is what stops a later lane from 'improving' the score by copying these rows across.
_split_rule: blind iff sha1(code).hexdigest()[0] in '0123'. Deterministic, computed before any row was written, and re-checkable in one line - so the split cannot have been picked to flatter the result.
_source: UT Direct building information pages, no login. Page URL per row below; the photographs themselves are NOT committed because UT Direct states no licence on them.

_kinds.canopy: a roof/blade/marquee/porte-cochere STANDS OVER the doors, cantilevered or on its own posts, separate from the mass
_kinds.arcade: a colonnade or covered walk runs in front and the doors open off it
_kinds.recess: the doors sit back under the building's own upper floors
_kinds.flush: a plain opening in the wall plane; nothing over it

rows.note: Batts Hall: a flush entrance in the limestone base.
BRB: a flush door bank in the base, nothing over it.
McCombs / CBA: a large white projecting roof plane with a red fascia band standing out over the whole glazed entrance front, above the door bank at the head of the steps.
CMB: a flush entrance under the metal-clad mass.
Chemical & Petroleum Engineering: a columned covered walk runs in front of the whole entrance wall.
CRH: flush doors in a plain brick wall.
Harry Ransom Center: the whole ground floor stands behind a colonnade of full-height piers; the entrance opens off it.
Jester Center: a run of arches along the base of the tower block; the doors open off the covered walk.
Littlefield House: a wraparound one-storey gallery on turned columns runs across the entrance front. The 1894 porch.
Main Building: the south entrance is under the seven-arch limestone arcade of the South Mall front.

Tom & Cinda Hicks North Gate: two full-height brick piers, a continuous bronze-tinted glass curtain wall on a mullion grid recessed between them, a gold-lettered signage band across the head, a UT roundel above the doors, a limestone plinth in front. NOTHING PROJECTS from the elevation. This is the building the previous round called family D's win while family D was stamping a 3.20 m steel blade on it.

Bass Concert Hall / PAC: the door bank sits back behind a row of white piers under the overhanging glass box; nothing cantilevers over the doors themselves. The white projecting plane in the photograph is the roof, five storeys up.
San Jacinto Garage: a plain vehicle opening.
Student Services Building: a recessed ground floor under the limestone mass.
SW7: a flush door in a white masonry wall with an external stair beside it.
SWG: a plain vehicle opening in the concrete frame.
Sanchez Building: a flat brick-and-glass elevation with a long ramp; nothing projects over the entrance.
TCC: a colonnade across the entrance front, doors behind it.
Texas Memorial Museum: bronze doors flush in the limestone at the head of the terrace steps.
A small flat canopy on two posts over a recessed entrance in a brick wall.
A full porte-cochere: a deep flat canopy with a ribbed metal fascia spanning the whole entrance drive, recessed downlights in the soffit, doors set back under it.
Waggener Hall: a portal at the head of a double stair, carved surround, flush in the wall.
